correctness.rationale: The exact grid second/fourth moments orthogonalize 1, s and s²-μ₂; the resulting quadratic reproducing kernel gives the boundary evaluation weights. Its two roots lie on the interval for m≥2. A finite polynomial summation between those roots proves the Bernoulli-root identity exactly (including root/grid coincidences). Uniform bounded periodic Bernoulli terms give the O(m⁻³) asymptotic, and the irrational progression on m=2 mod 5 proves the entire closed accumulation interval, not just bounds. The standalone checker passed 8,461 exact rational and high-precision assertions; finite checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Boundary evaluation of a degree-two least-squares regression under bounded response errors is a natural sharp stability invariant. Unlike a routine finite-grid matrix sum, the result gives a closed formula for arbitrary sample size and a full irrational arithmetic limit-set classification of its second-order error. It explains why there cannot be a fixed second-order finite-sample correction and provides directly attainable worst-case bounded-data amplification. It makes no unsupported extrapolation to the full polynomial projector norm.
